tagline: Global leader in financial services for institutional investors
hero_kpi_rationale: AUC/A (Assets Under Custody/Administration) is the primary driver for the company, as it generates the majority of recurring revenue through servicing fees. It is a key indicator of the company's leading global position in services for institutional investors.

kpis.name: Assets Under Custody/Administration
kpis.explanation: Total assets that the company manages or oversees for its institutional clients.
kpis.description: AUC/A increased by 16% in 2025, driven by rising markets and new client mandates.
kpis.signal: Strong growth driven by market performance and client flows

kpis.name: Total fee revenue
kpis.explanation: Revenue generated from custody, administration, foreign exchange, and securities financing services.
kpis.description: Fee revenue grew by 8% in 2025, supported by servicing, administration, and foreign exchange fees.

kpis.name: Net interest income
kpis.explanation: Difference between interest earned and interest paid on interest-bearing assets.
kpis.description: NII increased slightly due to growth in interest-earning assets, despite a 10 bp decline in NIM.

kpis.name: Pre-tax margin
kpis.explanation: Pre-tax profit divided by total revenue.
kpis.description: Pre-tax margin reached 26.8% in 2025, an increase of 70 basis points compared to 2024.

kpis.name: Return on average common equity
kpis.explanation: Net income available to common shareholders divided by average common equity.
kpis.description: Return on average common equity improved to 11.5% in 2025, up from 11.1% in 2024.

kpis.name: Total headcount
kpis.description: Total headcount was approximately 52,000 employees as of December 31, 2025.

risks.title: Intense competition and pricing pressure
risks.score_rationale: Mentioned first in strategic risks, with strong language ('intense', 'materially affect'). Pricing pressure is a recurring theme impacting margins and growth.

risks.title: Technological evolution and new entrants
risks.score_rationale: Highlighted as a major disruptive factor ('disrupt materially'). AI and DLT are explicitly cited as transformative technologies likely to disrupt the financial industry.

risks.title: Dependence on large institutional clients
risks.score_rationale: The text emphasizes the significant impact ('significant effect') of gaining or losing large clients on assets under management (AUM/AUC). Concentration is a key risk.

risks.title: Risks related to new product and service development
risks.score_rationale: The development of new products (Alpha, digital assets, AI) is presented as costly, dependent on third parties, and uncertain ('substantial risks and uncertainties').

risks.title: Risks related to acquisitions and strategic alliances
risks.score_rationale: Transactions (acquisitions, alliances) involve numerous challenges ('risks and financial, accounting, tax, regulatory challenges') and may not deliver expected benefits.

risks.title: Regulatory compliance and evolving legal framework
risks.score_rationale: Mentioned in the context of competition and new technologies ('evolving laws and regulations', 'regulatory frameworks'). The evolving framework for digital assets is specifically cited.

risks.title: Cybersecurity and IT resilience risks
risks.score_rationale: Explicitly mentioned in the context of acquisitions ('additional cybersecurity and resiliency risks'). Increased technological dependence heightens this risk.

ai_positioning.summary: State Street recognizes AI and distributed technology as major strategic threats that could materially disrupt its operations, financial markets, and servicing requirements. The rapid adoption of these technologies is explicitly cited in the risk factors, particularly in the context of competition.
evidence: Mentioned in Item 1A Risk Factors: 'adoption and implementation of evolving and emerging technologies, such as artificial intelligence and distributed ledger technology, and related regulatory frameworks, have the potential to disrupt materially the activities of the financial services industry'
Categorized as strategic risk alongside market competition and new market entrants
